**Title:** "The radial evolution of solar wind speeds"

**Authors:** S. L. McGregor, W. J. Hughes, C. N. Arge, D. Odstrcil, and Nathan A. Schwadron

**Journal:** *Journal of Geophysical Research-Space Physics* (American Geophysical Union), published March 31, 2011

**DOI:** 10.1029/2010JA016006

**Abstract (summary):** The authors use the WSA-ENLIL model to show that solar wind speed changes substantially between the outer corona (0.1 AU) and 1.0 AU and beyond, with most of the change occurring within a few tenths of an AU of the Sun. The effect is strongest during solar minimum for wind measured at 400 to 500 km/s at 1.0 AU. The fastest and slowest wind changes little, which the authors support with ionic charge state observations. They conclude that the intermediate-speed wind is a mix of originally fast and slow wind, implying a more bimodal solar wind in the corona than seen at 1.0 AU. For example, the paper notes that "the fastest and slowest solar wind experiences little acceleration or deceleration."

I can't reproduce the full abstract verbatim, but the complete text is available on the article's page at scholars.unh.edu/physics_facpub/77.

The paper is by R. C. Allen et al. and was published in *Astronomy & Astrophysics* in 2021 (vol. 650, A25). I didn't find an arXiv listing in these results, so I can't confirm an arXiv ID.

The authors built a catalog of Parker Solar Probe stream interaction region observations, paired with STEREO-A and with ACE and Wind at 1 au. The paper describes the event identification methodology, the initial catalog covering PSP orbits one through five with matching 1 au observations, and how to access the living catalog. A Harvard CfA summary says these missions measured and categorized the distances, pressures, magnetic fields, and speeds of eleven SIRs and CIRs, tracking their evolution over the course of almost two years. The stated aim is a catalog with strict identification criteria that supports both case studies and statistical work.

**Abstract (summarized):** The paper presents a "living catalog" of stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) observed by Parker Solar Probe (PSP). It pairs these with observations from STEREO-A and from ACE and Wind at 1 au. The authors describe their event identification method and the initial catalog covering PSP orbits one through five, and they explain how to access the catalog for future case and statistical studies.

  "message": "# Empirical solar-wind benchmarks for a 0.1–2.5 AU 3D MHD model

Most numbers below were read from the source text: full PDFs converted to text locally, PMC or HTML pages, or arXiv. Three markers are used:
- **[V]** verified from the primary text, with table, equation or section given.
- **[S]** taken from a secondary source that quotes the original; the original was not opened.
- **[U]** not verified. Abstract-level, a search-index snippet, or from memory.
- **"derived"** means I computed it from verified numbers.

## 1. Radial scalings, 0.1–1 AU and beyond

**Helios fast wind (v_R > 600 km/s).** Hellinger et al. 2011, JGR 116, A09105, doi:10.1029/2011JA016674, Sec 3.2, Eqs 5–6 [V] (http://space.asu.cas.cz/~helinger/hellal11.pdf).
- B ≈ 5.8 R⁻¹·⁶ nT and n ≈ 2.8 R⁻¹·⁸ cm⁻³, with R in AU.
- T∥ ≈ 2.7e5 R⁻⁰·⁵⁴ K, T⊥ ≈ 2.4e5 R⁻⁰·⁸³ K, T ≈ 2.5e5 R⁻⁰·⁷⁴ K.
- The authors read the slower-than-R⁻² density fall-off as possible deceleration of fast wind by stream interaction.
- Their heating model assumes a Parker field: B_r ∝ R⁻², B_t ∝ R⁻¹, 45° at 1 AU.

**Helios slow wind (v_R < 400 km/s).** Hellinger et al. 2013, JGR 118, doi:10.1029/2012JA018205, Sec 2.1, Eqs 3–4 [V] (http://space.asu.cas.cz/~helinger/hellal13.pdf).
- B ≈ 5.7 R⁻¹·⁶ nT and n ≈ 11 R⁻¹·⁹ cm⁻³.
- T∥ ≈ 8.1e4 R⁻⁰·⁵⁹ K, T⊥ ≈ 5.2e4 R⁻⁰·⁵⁸ K, T ≈ 6.2e4 R⁻⁰·⁵⁸ K.
- Table 1 [V] gives fits in six speed bins (200–300, 300–400, 400–500, 500–600, 600–700, 700–800 km/s):

| Bin (km/s) | 200–300 | 300–400 | 400–500 | 500–600 | 600–700 | 700–800 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| n₀ (cm⁻³) | 14 | 10 | 6.1 | 4.5 | 3.1 | 2.7 |
| ξ_n | −1.9 | −1.9 | −1.9 | −1.7 | −1.8 | −1.8 |
| T∥₀ (MK) | 0.049 | 0.081 | 0.15 | 0.24 | 0.29 | 0.32 |
| ξ∥ | −0.49 | −0.76 | −0.70 | −0.58 | −0.55 | −0.56 |
| T⊥₀ (MK) | 0.034 | 0.052 | 0.10 | 0.18 | 0.24 | 0.27 |
| ξ⊥ | −0.50 | −0.73 | −0.79 | −0.79 | −0.81 | −0.92 |

- Text: there are "indications of the overall acceleration of the slow solar wind streams".
- Sec 3.2: the expected Parker angle for 350 km/s at 1 AU is "about 50°". This is computed, not observed.

**Helios pure coronal-hole fast wind.** Perrone et al. 2019, MNRAS (arXiv:1810.04014), Table 3 [V].
- n_p = 2.37 R^(−2.02±0.05) cm⁻³ and n_pV_r = 1.53e3 R^(−1.99±0.05) cm⁻³ km/s. Proton flux × R² is conserved.
- B = 5.6 R^(−1.63) nT, |B_r| = 3.5 R^(−1.84) nT, |B_t| = 2.9 R^(−1.29) nT.
- T_p = 1.96e5 R^(−0.90) K, T∥ = 1.29e5 R^(−0.48) K, T⊥ = 2.3e5 R^(−0.99) K.
- Table 2 [S] quotes Totten et al. 1995 for 700–800 km/s: n −1.88±0.23, B −1.45±0.20, T_p −0.86±0.28, γ = 1.46±0.16.
- Text [S] quotes Khabarova & Obridko 2012 (ApJ 761, 82) over 0.29–5 AU: |B_r| ∝ R⁻¹·⁶⁶⁶ and |B_t| ∝ R⁻¹·⁰⁹⁶.
- Derived: at 1 AU, atan(|B_t|/|B_r|) ≈ 40° for this fast wind.
- The MNRAS volume and page (483, 3730) are from memory [U].

**Helios, all wind, 0.29–0.98 au.** Venzmer & Bothmer 2018, A&A (arXiv:1711.07534) [V].
- Table 3 gives median and mean fits:

| Quantity | Median fit | Mean fit |
|---|---|---|
| B (nT) | 5.38 r⁻¹·⁶⁵⁵ | 6.05 r⁻¹·⁵⁴⁶ |
| V (km/s) | 411 r⁰·⁰⁵⁸ | 436 r⁰·⁰⁴⁹ |
| n (cm⁻³) | 5.61 r⁻²·⁰⁹³ | 7.57 r⁻²·⁰¹⁰ |
| T (K) | 7.14e4 r⁻⁰·⁹¹³ | 9.67e4 r⁻⁰·⁷⁹² |

- Model, Eqs 12–19: v_slow = 363 r⁰·⁰⁹⁹ and v_fast = 483 r⁰·⁰⁹⁹ km/s. Derived: about +13% speed gain from 0.3 to 1 au.
- Model exponents: n ∝ r⁻²·¹¹, T ∝ r⁻¹·¹⁰, B ∝ r⁻¹·⁶⁶.
- A&A 611, A36 is from memory [U].

**PSP Encounter 1, about 0.17–0.5 au.** Huang et al. 2020, ApJS (arXiv:1912.03871), Table 1 [V].
- Slow wind (<450 km/s): T_p −1.34±0.12, N_p −2.38±0.28, B −1.83±0.06.
- Fast wind (>450 km/s): T_p −1.21±0.09, N_p −2.59±0.18, B −1.66±0.06.
- T falls more steeply inside 0.3 au than Helios shows beyond 0.3 au.

**PSP + Helios speed classes.** Dakeyo et al. 2022, ApJ 940, 130, doi:10.3847/1538-4357/ac9b14 (arXiv:2207.03898) [V].
- Five populations A–E span 250–700 km/s in Helios data. "The slower the wind is, the more progressive is its acceleration", while E is about constant over 0.3–1 au. The km/s gain per class is shown only in Fig. 1a, not in the text [U].
- Table 1, A→E: γ_p = 1.57, 1.59, 1.52, 1.44, 1.35 and γ_e = 1.29, 1.24, 1.23, 1.23, 1.21.
- Iso-poly model speeds at 1 au: 292, 354, 406, 488, 634 km/s.
- Derived, using their n ∝ r⁻²: T_p ∝ r^(−2(γ_p−1)), so α_p runs from −1.14 (A) to −0.70 (E).

**Speed evolution in a model.** McGregor et al. 2011, JGR, doi:10.1029/2010JA016006 [S, abstract].
- This is a WSA-ENLIL result, not data. Most speed change happens within a few tenths of an AU. It is largest for 400–500 km/s wind at 1 AU, and the fastest and slowest wind change little.
- Schwenn 1990 slow-wind acceleration numbers and Maksimovic et al. 2020 class speeds: [U], full texts blocked.

**Open flux.** Badman et al. 2021, A&A 650, A18 (arXiv:2009.06844), abstract [V].
- PSP shows r²|B_r| conserved down to 0.13 AU, with best estimate about 2.5 nT AU².

**Ulysses fluxes per steradian.** Verscharen et al. 2021, MNRAS 506, 4993 (arXiv:2107.06540) [V].
- Mass flux F_m mean = 3.55e-16 au² g cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹ (solar minimum, scan 1). Polar wind ≈ 3.5e-16 (scan 1) and ≈ 2.2e-16 (scan 3). Derived: n_p v ≈ 2.1e8 cm⁻² s⁻¹ at 1 AU.
- Polar momentum flux F_p ≈ 2.5e-8 (scan 1) and 1.7e-8 (scan 3) au² g cm⁻¹ s⁻² sr⁻¹. Derived: ρv² ≈ 2.5 and 1.7 nPa at 1 AU.

**Typical 1 AU values.**
- Venzmer & Bothmer Table 1 [V], OMNI hourly 1963–2016:
  - Medians: B 5.66 nT, V 408.5 km/s, n 5.28 cm⁻³, T 7.47e4 K.
  - Means: 6.16 nT, 418 km/s, 6.48 cm⁻³, 1.13e5 K.
  - Two-lognormal speed peaks at 489 and 368 km/s.
- Jian et al. 2019 Table 2 [V], ambient wind: mean B 6.8 vs 5.26 nT, V 442 vs 401 km/s, P_dyn 2.27 vs 1.52 nPa (Cycle 23 OMNI vs Cycle 24 STEREO).
- Ebert et al. 2009, JGR 114, A01109 (Ulysses slow/fast tables): [U], paywalled. The abstract says slow-wind T_p falls off more gently with distance than fast-wind T_p.
- Lopez & Freeman 1986 T–V fits at 1 AU [U, abstract via search index; units of 10³ K inferred]:
  - V > 500 km/s: T = 0.77V − 265.
  - V < 500 km/s: T^½ = 0.031V − 4.39.
  - The 1987 erratum was not checked.
- Le Chat et al. 2012 [V] use T_p ≈ 0.5 V² (K, km/s) at 1 AU.

**Beyond 1 AU.** Voyager: Richardson et al. 1995 T ∝ R⁻⁰·⁴⁹ [U, secondary quote]. Elliott et al. 2012: a single linear T–V fit fails beyond about 2.5 AU [S, abstract].

## 2. n–v anticorrelation and energy/momentum-flux invariance

**Le Chat, Issautier & Meyer-Vernet 2012, Sol. Phys.** (arXiv:1203.1316) [V].
- Energy flux: W = ρV(V²/2 + GM☉/R☉).
- Sec 3.1, protons only, at 1 AU: ⟨W⟩ = (1.5±0.4)e-3 W m⁻². By spacecraft: Helios 1.4±0.2, Ulysses 1.7±0.4, Wind 1.3±0.3 (all e-3).
- Sec 3.3, with alphas (which add about 15%): ⟨W⟩ = (1.7±0.4)e-3 W m⁻² at 1 AU, which scales to 79 W m⁻² at 1 R☉.
- W is independent of speed and latitude to within 10%.
- Most probable value (Wind/3DP, 1994–2011): 8.5e-4 W m⁻², with FWHM range [4.1:16]e-4.
- Eq 3: ρ ≈ 1.7e-12 [V(V² + 3.81e5)]⁻¹, with ρ in kg m⁻³ and V in km/s. It fits the data up to 700 km/s.
- Table 1: slow wind (400 km/s) n 4.7 cm⁻³, T_p 0.8e5 K; fast wind (750 km/s) n 1.4 cm⁻³, T_p 2.8e5 K.
- Fig. 4, solar minimum 2007–2009: mean P_dyn is 1.57 nPa (Wind) and 1.70 nPa (Ulysses).
- Derived: Eq 3 gives a local slope dln n/dln V of −1.6 at 400 km/s and −2.2 at 750 km/s. ρV² is 1.28 nPa at 400 km/s and 1.35 nPa at 750 km/s, so momentum flux is close to constant. That supports the n v² = const boundary rule.

**PSP.** Liu et al. 2021, A&A (arXiv:2101.03121) [V].
- W normalized to 1 R☉ is 69.4 W m⁻², quoted as about 70±14 W m⁻². By encounter: E01 77.3, E02 59.4, E04 67.2, E05 73.6.
- W ∝ r⁻¹·⁹².

**Model boundary rules.**
- EUHFORIA (Samara et al. 2024, arXiv:2405.09693, Eqs 3–5, citing Pomoell & Poedts 2018) [V]:
  - n = n_fsw (v_fsw/v)², T = T_fsw ρ_fsw/ρ, B_r = B_fsw v/v_fsw.
  - Constants: v_fsw = 675 km/s, n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³, B_fsw = 300 nT, P = 3.3 nPa, T_fsw = 0.8 MK at 0.1 au.
- MS-FLUKSS (Hegde et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.22386, Sec II.4) [V]: N V_R² = N_min V_fast² and N T = N_min T_max, with N_min = 200 cm⁻³, T_max = 2 MK, V_fast = 700 km/s.
- ENLIL [U, search snippet of Odstrcil CCMC 2012 slides; the server returned errors]: momentum-flux balance N V^x with x = 2, and P_th = const. Fast stream 200 cm⁻³ and 1.0 MK for WSA at 0.1 AU. An older 2007 deck gives 300 cm⁻³ and 1 MK.
- Wang 2010 ApJL 715, L121 and Schwadron & McComas: [U], only secondary descriptions found (mass flux about constant at 1 AU).

## 3. SIR/CIR statistics versus distance

**Jian et al. 2019, Sol. Phys. 294:31, STEREO 2007–2016** [V] (doi:10.1007/s11207-019-1416-8).
- 575 SIRs, of which 8.7% are hybrids with ICMEs.
- 33% have shocks: 19% forward only, 10% reverse only, 4% pairs. Pristine SIRs: 30% (16%, 10%, 4%).
- Shock rate is 25% in Cycle 23 vs 32% in Cycle 24.
- Table 2, mean values, Cycle 23 (Wind/ACE) vs Cycle 24 (STEREO):

| Quantity | Cycle 23 | Cycle 24 |
|---|---|---|
| B_max | 15.5 nT | 13.3 nT |
| Pt_max | 175 pPa | 147 pPa |
| V_min | 357 km/s | 323 km/s |
| V_max | 587 km/s | 556 km/s |
| ΔV | 230 km/s | 233 km/s |
| P_dyn,max | 8.8 nPa | 7.3 nPa |

- Table 3: Np_max mean 33 cm⁻³ at STEREO-A vs 25 cm⁻³ at STEREO-B, 24±4% lower at STEREO-B (0.02–0.14 AU farther out).
- Acceleration rate across SIRs: 0.3–8.2 m s⁻².
- Sec 5: "rising from a shock rate of 3% at 0.72 AU … to 91% at 5.3 AU".

**Jian et al. 2006, Sol. Phys. 239, 337, 1 AU 1995–2004** [S].
- 365 SIRs, 24% with shocks (Henderson 2025).
- Richardson 2018: about 17% forward, about 6% reverse, 1.4% pairs.
- Derived: about 36 SIRs/yr, about 2.7 per rotation. Full text not accessed.

**Richardson 2018, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 15:1** [V] (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6390897/).
- Helios, inside 1 AU (citing Schwenn 1990):
  - About 25 candidate forward shocks, about 6 fully developed, and fewer than 10 reverse shocks.
  - That is about 2% forward and under 4% reverse, out of an assumed ~270 SIRs.
  - The closest SIR shock was at 0.63 AU.
- Richter et al. 1985: about 1 corotating shock per 200 days inside 0.5 AU, and 1 per 100 days or fewer at 0.5–1 AU.
- Pioneer: shocks "tend to form beyond 2 AU". By 3–5 AU, over 90% have forward shocks and about 75% reverse shocks.
- The Gosling & Pizzo 1999 thresholds were not checked directly [U].

**Henderson et al. 2025, ApJ 981, 87, MAVEN at 1.5 AU** [V] (doi:10.3847/1538-4357/adb03b).
- 185 SIRs from 2014–2023, mean duration 2.2 d.
- Raw shock rates: 10.3% forward, 3.7% reverse, 0.54% pairs.
- Corrected for MAVEN's partial solar-wind coverage: 55.9 ± 11.5%.
- Magnetic compression ratio H: 2.36±0.06 at MAVEN vs 2.08±0.06 at STEREO-A, ratio 1.18±0.05; 1.32 for the same SIRs seen at both.
- Compiled from earlier work [S]:
  - PSP, 0.15–0.78 au: 32 SIRs, 0 shocks (Allen et al. 2021, A&A 650, A25; full text not opened).
  - Pioneer Venus Orbiter, 0.72 AU: 203 SIRs, 3% with shocks.
  - Pioneer 11, 1–3 AU: 30 SIRs, 60% with shocks (Smith & Wolfe 1976).
  - Ulysses, about 5 AU: 54 SIRs, 91% with shocks.
  - Jian 2019 and Henderson give different letter suffixes (2008b vs 2008c) for the Ulysses paper.

**Geyer et al. 2021, A&A, Earth vs Mars 2014–2018** [V] (arXiv:2102.05948).
- 146 SIRs at 1 AU and 126 at 1.5 AU.
- Table 1 medians, 1 AU vs 1.5 AU:

| Quantity | 1 AU | 1.5 AU |
|---|---|---|
| v_max | 627 km/s | 505 km/s |
| v_min | 337 km/s | 356 km/s |
| n_max | 28.0 cm⁻³ | 12.5 cm⁻³ |
| B_max | 14.5 nT | 7.5 nT |
| T_p,max | 0.50 MK | 0.23 MK |
| Pt_max | 116 pPa | 32.2 pPa |

- Derived: n_max ∝ r⁻²·⁰, B_max ∝ r⁻¹·⁶, Pt_max ∝ r⁻³·².
- The stream crest broadens by about 17%; B and Pt broaden by about 45% around the stream interface.
- Table 2, aligned events, shock rates: Earth 13.3% (forward 6.7, reverse 6.7, pairs 0) vs Mars 35.6% (forward 20.0, reverse 6.7, pairs 8.9).

**Lai et al. 2010, STEREO SWG slides** [V, slides only].
- "SIR-driven shocks begin at about 0.4 AU" (https://stereo-ssc.nascom.nasa.gov/meetings/SWG/SWG_Mar_2010/Interplanetary_Shocks_Inner_Solar_System.pdf).
